items.headline: CBP to Launch CAPE Phase 2 for Reconciliation Entries June 29
items.summary: CBP informed the Court of International Trade on June 9 that CAPE Phase 2, covering reconciliation entries worth $28.7 billion in refunds, will launch June 29. Over 16 million entries have been processed to date with $22 billion in refunds sent to Treasury. DOJ continues to oppose lifting the suspension of immediate compliance requirements.

items.headline: CAPE Phase 3 for Finally Liquidated Entries Scheduled End of July
items.summary: At the June 9 CIT hearing, CBP testified that Phase 3 covering finally liquidated entries will be ready by end of July 2026. However, DOJ argues CBP cannot issue refunds on these entries without individual CIT lawsuits. The technical capability is on track but legal disputes continue at Federal Circuit.

items.headline: Trump Administration Appeals CIT Universal Refund Order to Federal Circuit
items.summary: DOJ formally appealed Judge Eaton's universal IEEPA refund order to the Federal Circuit, challenging the CIT's authority to order refunds for non-litigants with finally liquidated entries. The appeal also contests the order compelling CBP Commissioner Scott's testimony, creating new uncertainty for the refund process.

items.headline: CBP Reports $89B in CAPE Refunds Accepted, $24B Processed
items.summary: Latest CBP statistics show more than $89 billion in potential and certified IEEPA refunds accepted for processing through CAPE, with nearly $24 billion sent to Treasury for payment. CBP projects reaching $60 billion by month-end and plans $480 million in weekly Treasury transfers.

items.headline: Nike Hit with $1B Class Action Over IEEPA Tariff Refunds
items.summary: Nike faces consumer class action in Portland federal court alleging the company raised prices to offset $1 billion in IEEPA duties but won't return refunds to customers. This follows similar suits against Amazon, Lululemon, and other major retailers creating 'double recovery' litigation risk for companies pursuing federal refunds.

items.headline: Section 122 Replacement Tariffs Set to Expire Without Congressional Action
items.summary: The 15% Section 122 tariffs that replaced IEEPA duties expire July 24, 2026 unless Congress acts. No extension legislation has been introduced, potentially creating a tariff vacuum for non-Section 232/301 goods. Administration prefers permanent statutory replacement but faces uncertain Congressional politics.
